subject: Global fleet fallback lanes and resilience buffer — HelixAI dedicated request
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@helixai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@helixai.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix expansion + resilience lanes

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks for the time last week. We're moving faster than planned on our teleport feature and need a dedicated footprint conversation. High level: we expect sustained 2.5M tokens/day in US production in steady state, burst up to 5M tokens/day for new feature experimentation, and a mirrored footprint for EU with slightly lower baseline (~1.2M tokens/day). APAC launch is targeted Q4 and we expect an initial 400k tokens/day.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provision a tri-region dedicated plan with explicit resilience/swapping lanes so traffic can failover between US/EU/APAC automatically when capacity is constrained?
- We need a buffer policy for at least 1.5x baseline for the first 90 days post-launch and clear lead times for committed pool ramp.

I've attached Helix_requirements_v2.xlsx with traffic profiles and SLA constraints. Procurement (procure@helixai.com) is copying to start contract timelines.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform 
HelixAI

Attachments: Helix_requirements_v2.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@helixai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix expansion + resilience lanes

Sam —

Appreciate the details and the workbook. Short answer: yes, we can design a tri-region dedicated plan that includes automated failover "swap lanes" and a temporary buffer policy. A few clarifying/operational items before I spin up scenarios:

- Can you confirm peak sequence length distribution and planned concurrency per route (in the workbook we have a coarse estimate)?
- Are you OK with a canary rollout sequence (US canary -> EU -> APAC) to surface performance regressions before full shift?
- Any hard constraints on encryption/key residency for EU/APAC (affects Private vs Dedicated options)?

I'll loop Irene (capacity planning) to produce sizing scenarios and tradeoffs (baseline, 1.5x buffer, and a swap-lane-first-failover design). Marissa — can your team confirm procurement timelines so we can map ramp milestones into the contract?

Connor O'Brien
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix expansion + resilience lanes

Irene / Rishi —

Forwarding Helix request. They've asked for tri-region dedicated with swap lanes and a 1.5x resilience buffer for 90 days. Key asks above. Please run three scenarios and attach a quick matrix:

- Scenario A (Conservative): baseline provisioning per workbook + 20% buffer, staged across regions (US primary).
- Scenario B (Resilience buffer): baseline * 1.5x with pre-wired swap lanes and 48-hour burst headroom.
- Scenario C (Cost-optimized swap): smaller committed pools + aggressive cross-region swap lanes and on-demand burst for experimental traffic.

Deliverable: per-region GPU counts (v100-equivalent), estimated sustained throughput (req/s), expected per-token cost delta vs hosted, rollback plan, and lead times for pool commits. Put numbers in connor_fallback_matrix.xlsx and push back any blockers. I put Marissa on cc for procurement ETA.

Thanks —
Connor

Attachment: connor_fallback_matrix.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix expansion + resilience lanes

Connor —

Attached is the sizing_scenarios.csv and a short rationale. Summary below (high level):

- Scenario A (Conservative): US 12 gpus (sustained ~1.8M tokens/day), EU 6 gpus, APAC 2 gpus. Buffer ~20% covers expected growth for 60 days. Lead time for committed pool: 6 weeks.
- Scenario B (Resilience 1.5x): US 18 gpus, EU 9 gpus, APAC 3 gpus. Swap lanes configured with hot re-routing; we estimate an effective failover headroom of ~1.4x per region because of cold-cache penalties on first requests. Lead time: 8–10 weeks for full pre-wiring and canary configs.
- Scenario C (Cost-optimized swap): US 10 gpus committed + 6 on-demand burst nodes; EU 5 committed + 3 burst; APAC hybrid edge nodes (1 committed). Lower committed cost but relies on our burst inventory; higher failure risk during simultaneous regional surges.

Tradeoffs & notes:
- Cross-region KV cache sync is the single biggest risk for latency-sensitive routes. Swap lanes will succeed functionally but may show tail-latency spikes on first request after failover.
- If Helix requires zero-notice failover within 30s, we recommend Scenario B + Cloud-provider reserved capacity overlay (adds ~12% cost).
- If they want encryption key residency in EU, that pushes towards a Private/dedicated control plane for EU — adds configuration lead time and legal review.

I put per-GPU throughput and cost deltas in the CSV. Ping me for a quick call — I can walk through the numbers.

Irene Choi
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sizing_scenarios.csv

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@helixai.com>, procure@helixai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix expansion + resilience lanes

Sam / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Based on Helix's profiles and our capacity work, recommended path is Scenario B (Resilience 1.5x) with a staged canary:

1) Canary window (2 weeks): US-only canary at reduced % of traffic to validate KV cache behavior and tail-latency under swap lanes.
2) EU roll (3 weeks after canary start): bring EU committed pool online, run geo-routing and legal/key checks.
3) APAC soft launch (4–6 weeks after EU): smaller committed footprint with on-demand burst enabled.

Key asks for procurement/signature:
- Approval for 90-day resilience buffer billing terms (we'll bill committed pool at 1.5x baseline for first 90 days, then re-evaluate).
- Agreement on canary plan and SLA wiggle-room for initial tail-latency during failover.

Next steps: Marissa will push a contract addendum and timeline. I've attached the matrix and the sizing CSV for reference. I'll create a DocuSign for the buffer term and share a HubSpot milestone (link below). If you're good with the canary cadence, we can target US canary week-of May 10th.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: connor_fallback_matrix.xlsx, sizing_scenarios.csv
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/DEAL-7842, DocuSign: https://docusign.com/xx/helix-buffer-addendum
